messages:
dana: quick idea: instead of merging whole adjacent shards for warmstart, what if we do tensor-granularity concat across shard boundaries for tiny tensors only? could reduce read amplification without large buffer copies.
mike: interesting. so loader would read segments that correspond to multiple tiny tensors and stitch them into one buffer, but leave big tensors alone?
dana: exactly. tiny = <8KB or user-configurable. keeps large tensors out of the concat path. less memory pressure than shard-merge.
yasmin: safetensors-specific: headers include tensor name/shape/offset. If we don't rewrite files, loader needs a virtual header map. doable by exposing a per-load remap descriptor.
todd: concern: cross-shard ordering. how do we guarantee same deterministic layout for the runtime remap so caches/kvcache offsets match between nodes?
dana: plan: remap descriptor is derived deterministically from manifest order + shard indices. it's a stable virtual layout; we sign it with manifest version so other nodes compute same remap. no artifacts rewritten.
mike: what about delta-rollouts where new model adds a tensor in the middle? remap would change and could invalidate caches. need a version pinning strategy.
yasmin: we already pin model version in serving. if remap changes across model-version, KV cache keys include model_version so eviction isn't broken.
dana: proof-of-concept API sketch: 
```
loader.load(model, opts={tensor_merge_policy: 'tiny-first', tiny_threshold: 8KB, max_concat_bytes: 512KB}) -> {remap_descriptor}
// remap_descriptor: base64-encoded stable table (virtual_offset -> shard,orig_offset,tensor_name)
```

todd: runtime perf: concatenating many tiny reads can improve IOPS but increase CPU work and memcpy. need benchmarks.
mike: also consider doing this incrementally: stream tiny tensors into preallocated pages and publish them as they arrive so KV lookups can start.
dana: yes, incremental publish is a goal. streamed concat + per-tensor ready flags. reduces tail latency.
yasmin: security/compliance: if we expose remap_descriptor we must avoid leaking internal path details. descriptor can contain shard-id hashes only.
dana: agreed. include only content-addressed ids (sha256 prefix) in descriptor.
infra-bot: note: new feature "tensor_merge" flagged as experimental. ops toggle available in staging.
mike: testing: we should fuzz tensor boundary cases (zero-length, misaligned padding, tensors split across 3+ shards). also test concurrent warmstart + eviction interleaving.
dana: unit test idea: synthetic manifest with repeating tiny tensors and a few large ones. verify remap produces identical tensor bytes as naive multi-read.
todd: metrics to add: `warmstart.tensor_merge.bytes_concatted`, `warmstart.tensor_merge.concat_ops`, `warmstart.tensor_merge.fallback_count`, `warmstart.tensor_merge.latency_ms`.
yasmin: fallback triggers: if concat buffer would cross a big-tensor boundary OR if mem_budget_exceeded -> skip concat for that group. log reason tag.
dana: CLI preview tool: `rwd-warm tensor-preview --model m:v1` prints groups with tensor names + orig shards + estimated savings. good for SRE review.
mike: API/manifest extension? maybe optional `tensor_merge_allowed=true/false` in model manifest. but default runtime heuristic is fine.
yasmin: can we reuse existing safetensors indexer soon? it already parses headers cheaply; hook into that parse to build merge groups without extra IO.
dana: yes reuse indexer. reduces work.
infra-bot: canary scheduled on `stg-ml-warm-1` for 2026-04-12T09:00Z. will run for 2h and collect p95/p99 for short/long sequences.
todd: rollout checklist: feature-flag, per-worker mem cap, perf traces, CLI preview, unit+fuzz tests, canary.
dana: I'll open a PR with the remap descriptor proto and a minimal concat runner + tests. tagging @mike for review.
mike: ack, will review. prioritize fuzz tests and a small perf harness.
yasmin: one more edge case: compressed bundles (gz/tar). concatenation across compressed streams not feasible without decompressing full region. skip concat for compressed shards.
dana: noted. skip compressed streams and emit metric `tensor_merge.skipped_compressed`.
infra-bot: canary results (prelim): tensor_merge applied to 64% of warmstarts, p95 short-seq -6%, p99 unchanged, cpu +2%, concat_ops avg 12 per warmstart. follow-up run recommended with larger concat pool.
dana: nice. i'll iterate on memory reuse and incremental publish semantics. thanks all for quick feedback! :rocket:
